name: TASTE
summary: A Russian medium-scale solar-axion telescope concept that also discusses Galactic-axion searches using its magnet.
detection_principle: Axion–photon conversion in a magnet with low-background X-ray detection; a dark-matter-halo mode requires a separate suitable detection configuration.

status.label: Public proposal / conceptual design
status.evidence: 2017 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: Towards a medium-scale axion helioscope and haloscope

collaboration.name: TASTE Collaboration / project team
lead_institutions: Institute for Nuclear Research of the Russian Academy of Sciences
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

key_parameters.name: Proposal stage
key_parameters.value: Early 2017 conceptual design; sensitivity and schedule are projections

results.summary: The paper presents infrastructure and conceptual design; no source sufficient to confirm construction and operation of the full apparatus was found.

science_scope: Primarily searches for solar-produced axions or hidden photons as complementary tests of dark-matter candidates. Solar flux is distinct from cold Galactic-halo dark matter; a solar-axion discovery alone would not establish the composition of cosmic dark matter.
